rationale: This is an equal-weight blend of two already-evaluated archive signals (Acquired_Intangible_Heavy_Base_Low_Gross_Profitability and Liquidity_Drain_Without_Margin_Cushion) sharing the identical gross-profitability conditioner, so it will almost mechanically land between their existing statistics and teach nothing new about the mechanism.

Internally consistent and a defensible economic reframing of the run-off story, but the two legs are mechanically linked (a firm not buying intangibles is by construction spending less cash), so the "conditional" structure risks being a near-degenerate restatement of a single non-acquisition state rather than an independent interaction.

The bounded revenue-drawdown conditioner is well-motivated by the prior FMB evidence and the sign logic is coherent, but this is now the fourth RANK(capx/ppent) × RANK(conditioner) construct in the archive and it overlaps materially with Three_Year_Capex_Program_With_No_Revenue_Response, so the incremental information is limited to whether a drawdown level beats a revenue change.

A genuinely unexplored second-moment construct with a coherent governance/monitoring rationale and a sign that matches the expression's natural direction; the main risk to diagnose is that capex-rate volatility proxies for firm size, age, and idiosyncratic volatility rather than allocation discipline.

The inventory-growth-minus-sales-growth leg is close to the published inventory-growth anomaly and the conditioner is essentially DuPont asset turnover, so novelty rests entirely on the interaction, but the leg itself is new to this archive and the design question (is the long side a general capital-discipline effect?) is legitimate.

This is an explicitly cosmetic variant of Labor_Bloat_Relative_To_Output_Low_Margin with only the conditioner swapped, and since gross-profit-to-assets and revenue-to-capital are highly correlated cross-sectionally, the result is very likely to replicate the existing signal without isolating anything economically new.
